findings.location: architecture/w03-plan/README.md 'Threads and W02d' ('No W02d change is needed'); plan.json:63 (threads.w02d), :65-82 (startupRecheck, startupConstraints)
findings.finding: The start-up re-check is accurate, but the claim that Rust plus musl fits NATIVE_STATIC with no W02d change misses two syscalls that are certain in steady state. (1) musl 1.2.5's mallocng realloc calls mremap(MREMAP_MAYMOVE) whenever the old and new sizes are both at or above MMAP_THRESHOLD (src/malloc/mallocng/realloc.c, branch 'use mremap if old and new size are both mmap-worthy'). Rust's default allocator on musl is musl malloc, so any Vec or String growing past about 128 KiB issues mremap. mremap is outside NATIVE_STATIC; only BROKER's filter has it, through the inherited worker superset (duty 23). EFFECT_GATE, OBSERVER, POLICY_WRITER and HOST_CONTAINMENT would be killed. (2) Naming a thread calls prctl(PR_SET_NAME=15): Rust 1.99 does so in sys/thread/unix.rs:412-425, reached from thread/lifecycle.rs:144-145, and musl's pthread_setname_np does the same for the current thread. NATIVE_STATIC has no prctl; BROKER allows only prctl(38). Common runtimes name threads by default; tokio, for example, names every worker and blocking-pool thread. Also, musl's abort and raise use tkill, not tgkill, so an abort becomes a SIGSYS kill rather than SIGABRT.
findings.requiredChange: Do not state 'No W02d change is needed' without qualification. Either add constraints the modules must keep: a global allocator that never calls mremap (or no reallocs above the mmap threshold), and unnamed threads only, with no runtime that names its threads. Or put a W02d reopening to the owner under W02d-Q2. Register the result as an obligation on HE-001 and T04.

findings.finding: Q-L approved four exact policy entries, but more of the closure is still unclassified under EXACT_SPDX_EXPRESSION. Exact expressions are also pinned in validate_reuse EXPECTED_DEPENDENCY_EXPRESSIONS, and allowedExceptionExpressions lists only 'Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception', 'Apache-2.0 OR BSD-2-Clause' and 'Apache-2.0 OR BSD-3-Clause'. (a) Rust std and core are 'MIT OR Apache-2.0' (library/std/Cargo.toml and library/core/Cargo.toml at b940084d) and are statically linked into every planned RUST_MUSL_STATIC module, so HE-001's license gate cannot pass. (b) libpathrs 0.2.6's crates, statically linked into runc: bitflags, itertools, libc, once_cell, thiserror and static_assertions ('MIT OR Apache-2.0'), memchr ('Unlicense OR MIT'), and rustix ('Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception OR Apache-2.0 OR MIT'). D-LIC-LIBPATHRS names the crate closure but reviews only libpathrs' own expression. (c) The GCC runtime (libgcc/libgcc_eh, GPL-3.0-or-later WITH GCC-exception-3.1) that gcc adds to static links (containerd static, runc static-pie, pause), as far as objects are pulled in. (d) nft's shared-library closure: libnftables, libnftnl, libmnl, gmp, and jansson, which kube-proxy needs because knftables runs `nft --json` (nftables.go:410,474).
findings.requiredChange: Put the additional expressions, or a reviewed OR-choice evaluation rule, to the owner, and widen D-POLICY-AMEND and LIC-HOST to match. Make D-LIC-LIBPATHRS list its crate expressions. Add an obligation that LIC-HOST, in its widened form, precedes HE-001's license gate.

findings.finding: (a) The re-check depends on W02d v2 (MET-ENFORCE-018), which is not merged. The NATIVE_STATIC in this tree (architecture/seccomp-allowlists/allowlists.json) has ppoll but no poll. On x86_64, musl's poll() (src/select/poll.c) and __libc_start_main's AT_SECURE check (:47-48) both issue SYS_poll, which would be killed today. The register has no obligation for W02d v2 to merge first, and w03_plan.py checks against the pre-v2 allowlists. (b) The gettid citation points at library/std/src/sys/thread/mod.rs, which only re-exports. current_os_id is at library/std/src/sys/thread/unix.rs:330-347 and is called from library/std/src/sys/pal/unix/stack_overflow/thread_info.rs:112-113. The rest of the re-check holds: the init order is unchanged; poll and the 1.99 dup are as stated; install_main_guard_linux_musl returns None; gettid is new in 1.99 on spawned threads only; cleanup is removed. (c) The musl 'patches' list names two CVEs, but musl.sh:36-59 at b940084d also applies the CVE-2025-26519 patches, and musl-toolchain.sh adds its patches as 0003/0004 after musl-cross-make's own.
findings.requiredChange: Register 'W02d v2 merged with poll in NATIVE_STATIC' as a precondition of HE-001 and T04, and have w03_plan.py check for poll once v2 is merged. Correct the current_os_id citation and the musl patch list.

findings.finding: Probes still accepted by backend_distribution.py: Q-L 'L-b' with approved official-binary reviews, because the binding only tests != PENDING; Q-E 'E-b' with etcd v3.7.2; etcd reset to v3.6.15 under Q-E E-a; a DATASTORE part from k3s-io/kine; an arm64 source that is the amd64 URL plus ' arm64', because the architecture check is a substring match; and every license review and host dependency removed. The policy is parsed with plain SafeLoader, so duplicate keys silently take the last value, and YAML errors raise yaml.YAMLError rather than the ValueError the README promises. The policy is also not pinned by digest. Probes accepted by w03_plan.py: thread flags are a recorded string not tied to musl, so 0x7d4f00 (which adds CLONE_VFORK) and 0x10900 both pass; the Rust commit is not tied to the version, so 1.90.0's 1159e78c passes as 1.99.0; musl patches and source are unchecked; result W02D_CHANGE_NEEDED passes while the README says no change; line numbers and anchors are unchecked (README.md:99999 and selection.json:D-NOPE pass); sources outside architecture/ are never checked; '..' in a source path reads outside the repository, failing with FileNotFoundError; integer flags raise TypeError; and a W03 obligation can be assigned to R12.
findings.requiredChange: Bind the owner decisions to the selected parts. Make the architecture check use the URL's path component. Load the policy with a duplicate-key-refusing constructor and map YAML errors to ValueError. In w03_plan.py, tie the thread flags to musl's documented set, check line ranges and anchors, refuse '..', and convert all errors to ValueError. Otherwise, narrow the README and docstring claims to what is checked.
